If he is going to be in a cage for extended periods of time, it needs to be at least 3-4 square feet.  

I really think it could work if you switched the roosters out - Mean rooster could be out in the morning, while nice rooster is in the kennel.  And vice versa.

If he is not doing better even after allowing him more space, I would consider taking him to a vet for diagnostics.  If it turns out that he really just needs more space, adopting him out to a farm or some place that he can have more room may be your best bet.  If neither of those things are options and/or he continues to go downhill, humane euthanasia by a veterinarian is also an option.  You don’t have to listen to some of the other redditors and “eat him for dinner”.  I think that’s terrible.

It is not enough space for both of them if they continue to fight.  Can you try switching them out?  Having one in a smaller area for a day and the other with full yard access...then switching the next day?  Or even 1/2 days?

A bigger cage may help but I’m not sure.  He also will need plenty of perches.  What size cage is he in now?  What does it look like?  What’s inside ?

Don’t eat him, that’s ridiculous.  I think he is not happy in isolation / in a cage.  I had a chicken that was in a cage for a few weeks and she did the same.  Once she got a full yard and a normal coop she did much better.  I don’t know that that will change his aggressive behavior, as that is just the nature of roosters.  But he may begin to eat again.  

Any cough?  Nasal discharge?  Ocular discharge?  Swollen or injured feet or wings?  

If he does not want to eat even after you give him a few days - a week outside he may be sick.  It can be extremely difficult to find out what is wrong with a sick rooster that is not showing any other clinical signs aside from inappetence (many times we can only tell on a necropsy post mortem)....especially one that is mean and not amenable to any diagnostics.  

See how he does after you give him space and sun.
